setup.why: Cross-check that list_users' data is truly workspace/group-scoped rather than implicitly filtered by the supplied project_id, by comparing against the project-independent group user listing.

attempts.changed: n/a - succeeded on first attempt using the fixture's v1 integer project id

top_level.users: array<object>, 12 items, ordered alphabetically by full_name, unpaginated

users[].browserstack_user_id: integer (BrowserStack account id, distinct from id)

myself.email: ABSENT in this response (declared as optional property, not in required[]; get_group_users_v2_v1's myself DOES include email for the same caller, confirming it's an optional/reduced-record omission, not an error)

illustrative_row.note: this is the fixture's own service account, also the caller (myself.id == 2522)

notes: Scoping: list_users is ACCOUNT/WORKSPACE-scoped, not project-scoped, despite requiring a project_id path param. The contract states project_id 'gates access only; the returned list is not filtered to this project's members', and this was verified empirically: invoking get_group_users_v2_v1 (which takes no project id at all and is explicitly group-scoped) against the same account returned the identical 12 users with identical fields and the same group_id (2615) as list_users. So project_id here functions purely as an access/permission check, not a filter - same 'no real project scope' pattern flagged for list_configuration_groups, except list_users does require a project_id argument where list_configuration_groups apparently requires none. project_id form: only the v1 INTEGER id was tested (379335744, from the fixture pool) and it worked on the first attempt; the contract explicitly types project_id as 'integer' (example 11046), so the v2 identifier form (PR-2005) was not attempted - not needed to answer the question and would contradict the declared type. User id form returned throughout: 'id' is a small TM-internal integer (e.g. 2522, 3741, 5465, ...), separate from 'browserstack_user_id' (also integer, e.g. 6013, 13450). Both are integers, never USR-NNN or email strings. Probe account's own user: id=2522, browserstack_user_id=6013, full_name='ing', email='probe-user@example.invalid' (myself.id in the list_users response matches this). Total active user count in the account: 12 (unpaginated, no truncation observed). No role field is present anywhere in the response, matching the contract's own guidance ('No role field'). Declared schema and actual response matched exactly in both directions - no drift found for this capability.
